correctness.rationale: Under positive affinities, K_N/N->kappa<1 bounds any target probability by B/N and drives the maximal degree to o_P(N) on each finite time horizon. Thus class-target probabilities converge uniformly to U_ac. The bounded-jump martingale has quadratic variation O(1/N), giving the class-edge ODE by a Lipschitz argument away from zero discordance. Two classes have constant successful rewiring rate and a stopped linear law; three-class matchings yield exact normalized initial drift 50/33 versus 5/3. The included exact-rational generator checker passes, but finite tests are not offered as the fluid proof.

originality.rationale: The closest full-text source establishes the precise homophilic threshold rewiring model and develops a representative-step-graphon scalar approximation, explicitly leaving rigorous microscopic convergence unproved. It does not imply the exact sparse class-edge fluid process or sharp universal two-class/three-class split. Prior adaptive voter and adaptive bounded-confidence models have state updates and different generators. Search and implication comparisons found no earlier equivalent claim among inspected sources; the unsurveyed literature, especially a 2025 fixed-states model, leaves residual priority risk.
residual_risks: No comprehensive priority search of every older adaptive rewiring paper can be claimed; a general class-type Markov population theorem may exist outside inspected literature.
Full text of arXiv:2511.15043 was not materially inspected; its similar fixed-state subject may require an independent priority check.
The no-self-loop convention differs by an asymptotically negligible term from the formal normalization in the cited generator; the finite rational example uses the explicitly declared convention.

value.rationale: The source proposes concordance as an effective collective coordinate. A universal exact scalar closure is a meaningful structural question: if true it supports model reduction over arbitrary sparse graph states; if false it specifies the missing observables. This theorem proves the exact two-class scalar regime and a minimal three-class failure at order-one drift, not a routine parameter substitution or small finite numerical improvement. The typed-edge fluid law provides a natural replacement without asserting the paper's approximate closure fails on typical data.
